title: Ops scrumlet: routing backlog & quota observations (2026-06-21)
content:
Summary:
Quick mid-month scrumlet (15 min) focused on a few noisy signals from last week's routing experiments and quota throttling during overnight windows. Goal: sync on who owns follow-ups and capture a lightweight action list.

Attendees:
- Aisha (owner)
- Miguel
- Liu
- Hannah
- (joined late) Priya (SRE)

Pulse / What changed since last check:
- Routing experiment "prefer-local-az" (A/B) rolled for 3 days: saw small latency wins for bursty short requests but unexpected imbalance in KV-cache hitrates causing extra GPU warmups.
- Quota enforcement spike: several customers experienced transient 429s between 02:00-03:30 UTC on 2026-06-19; root cause appears to be a regeneration race in quota tokens service when autoscaler bumped pods.
- Auth ping latency: p99 auth round-trip increased from 22ms -> 40ms for a 1-hour window during the same autoscaler event (possible cross-calls between auth and quota).

Details / Evidence:
- Miguel: routing logs show 18% higher cache miss rate for short sequences (<32 tokens) on replica group B. PR #987 contains traces and histogram exports.
- Liu: quota service horizon shows token-regeneration bursts correlated with Kubernetes HPA scale-up events at ~02:10 UTC. Pod startup caused a short-lived TTL miscalculation leading to double-issuance checks and then temporary drop-in capacity reported to gateway.
- Hannah: traced increased auth RTT to a sync call auth -> quota -> auth when quota endpoint returned 503; retries added ~18ms per request.

Hypothesis (quick):
1) The routing policy that biases local AZs results in uneven distribution of prefix-cached KV pairs; when traffic shifts, some GPUs warm-up more often (cold token overhead).
2) Quota service race during pod scale-up leads to transient state mismatch; Gateway interprets as exhausted quota resulting in 429s.
3) Auth-service retry path amplifies the surface area.

Immediate mitigations tried (during call):
- Rollback prefer-local-az to baseline routing on Canary cluster B (Miguel) — rolled back 02:45 UTC; observed stabilization within 20m.
- Hotfix to quota registry added temporary in-memory guard to prevent double-issue logic; staged to canary (Liu).

Action items (owners + due):
- Miguel: run a focused load test that simulates short-sequence burstiness against prefer-local-az variant, capture KV cache heatmaps. Due: 2026-06-25.
- Liu: open a postmortem draft for 429 event, include timeline, k8s HPA events, pod logs, and quota-regeneration traces. JIRA-PLTFM-1423 assigned. Due: 2026-06-24.
- Hannah: propose an auth retry budget change to fail-fast on quota 5xxs to avoid long tail latency amplification (PR & proposal). Due: 2026-06-28.
- Aisha: coordinate with SRE (Priya) to add a short-term guard in the autoscaler (cooldown increase for quota-backed services) and record in runbook. Due: 2026-06-23 (in progress).

Decisions made:
- Do not proceed with prefer-local-az rollout beyond canary until cache warming strategies (prepopulate / soft-affinity) are in place.
- Temporary throttling suppression for long tail retries: auth will fail-fast on quota 5xx for 30s after detection.

Open questions / Risks:
- Could the quota double-issue be exacerbated by multi-region control-plane replication lag? (Liu to test config matrix).
- Risk of user impact if we increase autoscaler cooldown: may delay capacity for real spikes; need to tune with synthetic storm tests.
- We do not yet know if some customers saw correlated errors across models; need to check per-customer routing affinity.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Sketch: pre-warm KV cache by proxying small synthetic prefix requests when routing decision flips. Could be a low-cost background lambda.
- Consider a lightweight leader-election inside quota pods to serialize token-regeneration during scale events (cheap guard).

Follow-up meeting / handoff:
- We'll revisit the status in next weekly platform sync (2026-06-28). If postmortem shows customer-visible impact, schedule an incident review with CS.

Attachments / quick links: 
- Load traces: s3://redwood-platform-debug/runs/2026-06-19-prefer-local-az-traces
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pltfm/pull/987
- JIRA: JIRA-PLTFM-1423
- Slack thread: #pltfm-routing (pinned: June 19 autoscale spikes)

Misc (informal):
- Miguel: "noticed weird cold start behavior only for requests <32 tokens — feels like an LRU churn issue"
- Hannah: "auth retries noisier than I'd expect; short-circuiting might be the cheapest win"
- Liu: "postmortem will probably recommend a tiny quota registry guard and clearer scale-up checklist"

End of notes.

-- quick signoff: Aisha
